Source: news reporting on PizzaBurg; Group NEXIX site visit
Framework & method
We assessed PizzaBurg against Carroll’s four responsibilities,
using public reporting — not a company interview.
Economic
Stay profitable
PizzaBurg operates 22 outlets and employs about 1,000 people. Staying profitable is what makes every other responsibility possible.
Legal
Obey the law
We reviewed public sources only. We found no reporting either way, so we make no claim in this tier.
Ethical
Do what is right
PizzaBurg states a focus on an inclusive workplace and on reducing plastic. We found no published target or outcome for either.
Philanthropic
Give back
This is where the evidence is strongest: iftar pizzas for mosques, and Christmas distribution to disadvantaged children.
Framework: Carroll (1991) · assessed against public sources only
Reported practice · Community giving
PizzaBurg’s community giving is real and repeated —
but every instance we found falls at Ramadan or Christmas.
During Ramadan, PizzaBurg provides pizzas to mosques for iftar. At Christmas, its own employees dress as Santa Claus and hand out free pizzas to disadvantaged children.
The pattern
Both are real and repeated. Both fall on a single occasion in the calendar, and we found no follow-up reporting on either.
What we could not find
Any published account of how many people either programme actually reached.
Our site visit
We found no public photographs of either distribution — this is the outlet we visited.
Source: news reporting on PizzaBurg; Group NEXIX site visit
Reported practice · Workplace & packaging
PizzaBurg states a direction on hiring and on packaging —
but we found no published target for either.
Sourced online
The company’s own recycling bin, in an outlet.
Sourced online
A PizzaBurg poster advertising women-only roles at two outlets.
Source: third-party CSR write-up on PizzaBurg; photos sourced online
Our assessment · The numbers PizzaBurg does not have
The giving is visible. What we could not find
is any way to tell whether it is working.
0
Public CSR reports found
0
Stated targets found
0
Measured outcomes found
Third-party write-ups exist. In every public source available to us we found no CSR report from PizzaBurg itself — no stated target, no measured outcome, and no named CSR owner. That is the gap the next four proposals are written to close.
Group NEXIX assessment of public sources
Proposed initiative — 01 of 04
Buy 1 Give 1 would tie a donated meal to one menu item,
so giving no longer waits for Ramadan.
We propose a designated menu item that funds one donated meal every time it is sold.
Self-funding
It would scale with sales instead of competing with them, and would turn giving into a daily event rather than a seasonal one.
How we would know it worked
Meals funded per month, published — a number that does not exist today.
Sourced online
Illustrative of the mechanism — not a PizzaBurg programme.
Group NEXIX proposal — not a PizzaBurg plan
Proposed initiative — 02 of 04
Biodegradable packaging would put PizzaBurg ahead of the
policy direction, in a country where over half are under 25.
We propose fully biodegradable packaging across all outlets, plus an incentive for customers who return their boxes for recycling.
Moderate upfront
Bangladesh has signalled a policy direction against single-use plastics, and over half its population is under 25.
How we would know it worked
Share of outlets switched over, and how many boxes come back.
Sourced online
Fibre-based packaging of the kind the switch would move to.
Group NEXIX proposal · policy and population context from public sources
Proposed initiative — 03 of 04
Student Support is the only one of our four proposals
that also feeds PizzaBurg’s own hiring pipeline.
We propose scholarships, free meals and paid internships for financially disadvantaged university students.
Low, scalable
It could start with a handful of places and grow only once it works — recruiting from the same pool as the outlet roles PizzaBurg advertises publicly.
How we would know it worked
Places offered each year, and how many of those students later join PizzaBurg.
Our site visit
Group NEXIX at the outlet — students of the kind this proposal would fund.
Group NEXIX proposal — not a PizzaBurg plan
Proposed initiative — 04 of 04
Food Rescue would cost almost nothing;
what it would need is a food-safety handoff protocol.
We propose donating unsold, still-safe food to shelters at the end of each trading day.
Near-zero
What it would need is not money but a written food-safety handoff protocol agreed with the receiving shelter.
How we would know it worked
Meals redirected each week, and the disposal cost avoided.
Our site visit
Pizzas at the outlet — this is the food Food Rescue would redirect.

Group NEXIX proposal — not a PizzaBurg plan
Where we would start
Three of the four need a decision rather than a budget —
so we would begin with those.
01
Food Rescue
Near-zero cost, and the food is already being discarded. What it needs is a written safety protocol — that can be agreed in weeks.
02
Buy 1 Give 1
Self-funding from the sale that triggers it, so it never competes with the trading budget — and it produces a monthly number to publish.
03
Student Support
Low cost, and it can begin with a handful of places before it grows.
04
Green PizzaBurg
Last only because it is the one that needs real investment — easier to fund once the first three are running and being measured.
Group NEXIX recommendation — not a PizzaBurg plan
PizzaBurg already contributes to society through community support
and special-day initiatives.
We suggest four new CSR activities: Buy 1 Give 1, Green PizzaBurg, Student Support, and Food Rescue.
These initiatives can benefit both society and the environment.
Thank you.
